minutes.headline: Committee publicly grappled with backlash after a new hire withdrew amid a social-media firestorm over race and curriculum
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with public comment and extended committee reflection on a weekend social-media controversy after a newly selected hire withdrew amid online attacks referencing race, religion and curriculum rumors; members debated communications policy and hiring-policy gaps without taking a vote. A finance consulting firm (TMS) gave a long best-practices presentation on budget development, MUNIS use, personnel control ledgers and purchase-order controls, and the committee worked through an early draft of the FY26-FY35 capital plan, including the failing turf field drainage, a primary school generator, and Turkey Hill facility needs. The committee approved a letter asking the town to allocate an additional round of Chapter 70 funding to the school budget and approved minutes and warrants before adjourning.

watch_next: Capital plan vote targeted for the committee's first meeting in September
Chapter 70 allocation request goes to a November special town meeting

what_happened.line: Members spent an extended session addressing backlash after a newly selected hire withdrew amid online attacks referencing race, religion and curriculum rumors; no vote or policy change resulted.
A finance consulting firm walked the committee through budget development, MUNIS controls and purchase-order practices in an informational presentation.
The committee worked through an early draft of the FY26-FY35 capital plan, covering turf field drainage, a primary school generator and Turkey Hill facility needs.
The committee voted to approve a letter asking the town to allocate an additional round of Chapter 70 funding to the school budget.
Members directed staff to get vendor scoping on turf drainage and agreed to add formalizing the district's hiring policy to a future agenda.

why_it_matters: The hiring-controversy discussion touches how the district communicates about staffing decisions and whether a hiring policy gets formalized, an open item for a future meeting.

The capital plan touches building and infrastructure spending across ten years, including the turf field, a primary school generator and Turkey Hill needs, with a committee vote targeted for September.
The Chapter 70 letter touches how much state school aid the town appropriates to the school budget, a request headed to a special town meeting vote.
